input.quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.
input.rationale: Compliant at the preferred position; no redline proposed. Duration: the express conformance warranty for Deliverables runs for "ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later" — i.e. a 90-day period (spelled in words rather than digits, which is the sole reason the automated period check misread it), measured from the later of delivery or acceptance, so it is at least the preferred 90-day benchmark and in practice longer. For Hosted Services the warranty is expressed as a term-length period — "throughout the subscription term" — which under § 8.2 means the Order Form initial term plus successive twelve-month renewal periods (the Agreement itself running three years under § 8.1), exceeding the preferred 12-month software benchmark. Scope: professional and workmanlike performance by qualified personnel to industry standards (19.1); material conformance of Services and Deliverables to documentation and specifications (19.1–19.2); compliance with Applicable Law and no intentionally introduced malicious code (19.3); plus no mid-term functionality diminution and no copyleft contamination of Customer source code. Remedy: 19.4 gives prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, escalating to termination of the affected item and refund of Fees paid, and is expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims — a real remedy, not sole-and-exclusive repair. Disclaimer: 19.5 is mutual, limited to implied warranties, and expressly does not limit any express warranty, service level, indemnity or stated remedy, so it does not swallow the express warranty and no carve-out edit is needed. Only immaterial gaps remain (refund of "Fees paid" rather than "paid or payable"), which the playbook directs us to note rather than flag. Acceptance testing in § 6 reinforces the warranty.
